contributions: Provides a rigorous yet accessible introduction to real analysis with 295 worked examples and 761 numbered exercises
Emphasizes completeness and careful proofs while maintaining clarity for students transitioning from elementary calculus
Covers real-valued functions of one and several variables, Riemann integration, sequences and series, and metric spaces
limitations: Requires only standard elementary calculus as a prerequisite for Chapters 1-5, but acknowledges the transition from calculus to rigorous analysis is increasingly difficult for students. Chapter 8 requires completion of Chapters 1-5, and Chapters 6-7 require linear algebra knowledge. Some proofs are omitted as exercises.
methods: The book presents real analysis through a structured progression: Chapter 1 develops the real number system including the completeness axiom, Archimedean property, and density of rationals; Chapters 2-3 cover differential and integral calculus of one-variable functions rigorously; Chapters 4-5 extend to sequences, series, and multivariable real-valued functions; Chapters 6-7 treat vector-valued functions and multiple integrals; Chapter 8 introduces metric spaces.
results: The text proves fundamental theorems including the Heine-Borel theorem, Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem, triangle inequality (Theorem 1.1.1), Archimedean property (Theorem 1.1.4), and density of rationals in reals (Theorem 1.1.6). It contains 295 completely worked out examples and 761 numbered exercises. The treatment of improper integrals is noted as more detailed than most comparable textbooks.
tldr: This is an open-access textbook covering introductory real analysis from the real number system through metric spaces, designed for junior/senior mathematics majors.
